sections.title: Human Value and Multi-Agent Session Continuity

todos.content: Identify and correct the session-persistence discontinuity so a human can reliably return to Jasper, Coding, Research, and future agent-profile conversations, decisions, visual artifacts, and workspace context across server and UI restarts.
todos.notes: Top-priority blocker because session continuity preserves the human's prior worktime, attention, mental energy, and token cost. Root cause correction on 2026-08-02: the Docker PostgreSQL database retained Jasper thread 019fbf63-9194-7ca3-843d-1eea1acab82a with 91 checkpoints and retained the requested governance conversation 019fbf91-b2af-7012-83cf-2ca48ae09d88. A manually started langgraph dev process on the same port exposed a separate local catalog, creating a false appearance of data loss. Added a documented Agent Server custom /runtime-identity route marked only by the Docker deployment; the UI now verifies backend-postgres-v1 before constructing the LangGraph SDK stream and blocks unverified development runtimes. Removed the root README dev-server launch path, restored the Docker/PostgreSQL Agent Server, and verified the recovered Jasper thread through the API. Focused backend, TypeScript, production-build, lint, and browser guard tests pass. The broader acceptance remains: durable production backing must recover transcripts, all agent-participation records and delegations, many-to-many workspace relationships, decisions, model-use records, and visual artifacts after process and machine restarts. Governance reference: GOVERNANCE_FRAMEWORK.md.

todos.content: Define the production many-to-many Workspace, Session, WorkspaceSessionLink, and profile-agnostic AgentParticipation contracts so one workspace can retain many sessions, one knowledge-work session can reference several workspaces, and Jasper, Coding, Research, or any future approved profile can contribute with explicit roles, versions, delegations, revisions, time bounds, decisions, outcomes, and artifacts.
todos.notes: Keep portable workspace identity separate from device-local filesystem bindings. Agent participation uses stable profile IDs and versions rather than fixed Jasper/Coding/Research columns, preserving future profiles and historical readability. Git remains code authority; LangGraph checkpoints retain thread state; Store retains owner-scoped relationships and manifests. Do not infer a primary workspace or authorization to clone, bind, or modify it. Governance reference: GOVERNANCE_FRAMEWORK.md.

todos.content: Design a clear human-controlled review surface for sessions and workspaces showing names, editable summaries, observed active time, pauses, every participating agent profile and delegation, decisions, outcomes, artifacts, and cross-workspace relationships without productivity scoring or coercive optimization.
todos.notes: The human must be able to inspect, correct, export, archive, and apply retention choices to their own knowledge-work record. Observed, idle, paused, and inferred time must remain distinguishable. Governance reference: GOVERNANCE_FRAMEWORK.md.

todos.content: Define a workspace- and session-linked model-use evidence ledger that records model/provider, local or cloud execution, agent profile, workflow version, measured versus estimated tokens and resources, verification outcomes, and human selection decisions.
todos.notes: Use the ledger to help the human identify when deterministic workflows and as-built knowledge make a smaller model sufficient. Jasper may explain or recommend; only the model selector or an explicitly approved agent profile selects. Prefer existing local capacity, never encourage hardware purchase, never silently load or switch models, and never turn minimum compute into a score imposed on the human. Governance reference: GOVERNANCE_FRAMEWORK.md.

todos.content: Complete Coding and Research voice routing, Jasper specialist narration handoff, long-playback stability, local-model isolation, and concise recoverable failure handling.
todos.notes: Coding=Murrow_2 and Research/reference/Fact-Checker=Lorde routing, three-minute queue stability, cloud-only endpoint isolation, recoverable malformed visuals, provider sanitization, and durable voice manifests are implemented and tested. Restarted the UI and sidecar persistently, verified UI HTTP 200, 34 voices including Murrow_2 and Lorde, and generated 164,980 bytes of SSE audio for a short Murrow_2 smoke phrase without an LLM call. The requested devstral-small-2:24b-cloud entry was briefly configured but removed after the authoritative Ollama CLI reported that devstral-small-2:24b was retired on 2026-07-15; authenticated Cloud discovery currently offers qwen3.5:397b and kimi-k2.7-code as coding models. Unloaded mistral-small:22b from GPU and verified ollama ps is empty. Reverted an incorrect Cloud-only sidecar policy attempt: the sidecar remains discovery-only, while agent profiles and the UI selector own model choice. A real segmented Jasper-to-specialist narration handoff still needs an end-to-end live assertion before this item can be completed. Governance reference: GOVERNANCE_FRAMEWORK.md.

todos.content: Run focused unit and browser regressions, full backend and frontend suites, then all fifteen real smoke checks in order without mocked routes or dev-only runtime overrides.
todos.notes: Historical gates passed the frontend production build, generated-schema checks, TypeScript, 27 Playwright tests, Research citations, and Research visual placement. The latest focused Jasper suite passed 52 tests and an earlier full backend run passed 236. This gate is currently open: live repository grounding passes, but grounded visualization regressed—Jasper reads repository files without calling draw_concept_map or publishing an artifact. The final ordered no-mock sweep must be rerun after the Jasper contract is corrected, and still requires the segmented handoff and continuous real three-minute audio run. Governance reference: GOVERNANCE_FRAMEWORK.md.

todos.content: Fix normal Agent Server execution without allow-blocking, Python 3.11 schema compatibility, stale-thread recovery, and prevent internal JSON/tool envelopes from leaking into visible chat.
todos.notes: Removed the blocking eager workspace fallback, migrated runtime TypedDict schemas to typing_extensions, sanitized stale-thread and provider errors, stopped subgraph streaming, filtered outer messages to the final assistant response, and defaulted internal tool calls to hidden. todos.notes: Replaced the custom JasperToolContractMiddleware and hidden task rejection with an agent-scoped LangChain create_agent graph plus the official Deep Agents SubAgentMiddleware. todos.content: Render model narration as a clickable sentence-level transcript linked to stable NarrationCue segment IDs.

todos.content: Expose the exact transcript sentence currently being spoken using authoritative playback state rather than elapsed-time guessing.
todos.notes: Acceptance: the indicator advances only when the corresponding cue begins, remains correct through pause and resume, and clears on stop, cancellation, completion, or playback failure. Governance reference: GOVERNANCE_FRAMEWORK.md.

todos.content: Support pause, resume, and playback beginning from any sentence in the transcript.
todos.notes: Use the renderer-neutral NarrationTrack/NarrationCue contract and retained audio/playback offsets. Acceptance requires correct continuation after pause and deterministic restart from every tested sentence. Governance reference: GOVERNANCE_FRAMEWORK.md.

todos.content: Add soft, visually calm highlighting transitions for the active transcript sentence and its associated visual node.
todos.notes: Avoid harsh borders, flashing, rapid animation, and forced viewport movement. Respect reduced-motion preferences and verify that presentation changes never alter artifact content. Governance reference: GOVERNANCE_FRAMEWORK.md.

todos.content: Represent node selection as evidence of human attention, never as authorization or an instruction that silently overrides the human's written or spoken prompt.
todos.notes: Persist active artifact and selected node as typed context distinct from messages and consent state. A related prompt may use the context; an unrelated or ambiguous prompt must not be reinterpreted to fit the selection. Governance reference: GOVERNANCE_FRAMEWORK.md.

todos.content: When selected-node context conflicts with or is ambiguous relative to the next prompt, pause and ask a neutral clarification before changing focus or acting.
todos.notes: Use a typed LangGraph interrupt with equally presented choices such as this node, another visual area, a side question, or a different concept/session. Silence and inaction are not consent; no option is inferred or preselected. Governance reference: GOVERNANCE_FRAMEWORK.md.

todos.content: Investigate and prove repeated draw_concept_map tool invocation and artifact publication within the same Jasper thread before enabling any automatic visual policy.
todos.notes: Known evidence to test: Jasper's prompt contains ambiguous 'call draw_concept_map once' wording; artifact recovery scans conversation-wide ToolMessages and keeps the first four; visual_artifacts currently has overwrite-style state; and a live ollama-cloud/glm-5.1 trace ended with a construction preamble instead of the registered tool call. Acceptance: in one fresh thread, create map A, focus or revise map A, create map B, inspect Studio traces for every expected tool call, refresh, and recall both artifacts without substitution or loss. Record model ID and response strategy for every run. Governance reference: GOVERNANCE_FRAMEWORK.md.

sections.title: Tent Poles — Memory Layer with Tools + Dashboard

todos.content: Design and document the Tent Poles memory layer: collaborative context compaction where Jasper proposes key load-bearing points (tent poles), user reviews/prioritizes, approved tent poles replace old messages. Concept doc with data structure, flow, storage, tools, UI, and open questions.
todos.notes: Concept designed. Tent poles = structural key points (decisions, facts, preferences, open questions, constraints). User co-creates and prioritizes. Replaces narrative summarization with collaborative context curation.

todos.content: DECISION: JSON file (tent_poles.json) at repo root — same proven pattern as todos.json. Survives restarts, simple to debug, no Docker/Postgres dependency. Migrate to LangGraph Store later for cross-thread semantic search if needed. Implement read/write helpers for tent_poles.json. Add GET /api/tent-poles endpoint to FastAPI sidecar (web_server.py) mirroring /api/todos pattern. Schema: {version, updated_at, updated_by, tent_poles: [{id, content, priority, scope: 'global'|'thread', thread_id?, created_at, updated_at}]}.
todos.notes: Implemented a validated TentPoleStore over root tent_poles.json with inter-process shared/exclusive locking, same-directory atomic replacement, file and directory fsync, restrictive permissions, scoped querying, mutation, and atomic batch reprioritization. Added GET/POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE FastAPI contracts with validation and stable errors.

todos.content: Phase 4: Define 4 LangChain @tool functions for tent pole management in backend/src/jasper_tools.py (NOT 5 — propose_tent_poles DROPPED per user decision). Tools: (1) set_tent_pole(content: str, priority: int, scope: str = 'global') -> str — add a tent pole; (2) update_tent_pole(id: str, content: str = '', priority: int = -1) -> str — edit/reprioritize; (3) remove_tent_pole(id: str) -> str — drop; (4) get_tent_poles(scope: str = 'all', thread_id: str = '') -> list[dict] — read current set. Tools read/write tent_poles.json. Jasper extracts key points IN-RESPONSE (not via a separate tool), presents to user, user approves on next turn, Jasper calls set_tent_pole for each approved item. Depends on jasper-react-loop.
todos.notes: Added the four specified LangChain tools with exact collaborative semantics, thread context isolation, stable JSON results, missing-ID handling, and active-only reads. Registered them in Jasper and the strict profile contract; no proposal-writing tool was introduced.

todos.content: DECISION: Second tab in existing right sidebar (next to Todos). Adapt todos/index.tsx pattern. Add tab toggle between 'Todos' and 'Tent Poles' panels. Poll /api/tent-poles every 3s (same as todos). Display tent poles grouped by scope (global vs current thread). Show: content, priority (sortable), scope badge. Inline edit for content. Drag-to-reorder for priority. Approve/reject buttons for pending proposals. Pending review indicator (badge count) in tab header.
todos.notes: Added a Todos/Tent Poles tabbed sidebar with global/thread grouping, scope/status badges, pending count, inline editing, proposal approve/reject, and drag reorder backed by one atomic priority transaction. Polling runs only while the sidebar is open. Playwright covers review, edit, approval, and reorder.

todos.content: DECISION: Hybrid scope — global facts (user preferences, project facts, long-term decisions) + per-thread decisions (conversation-specific choices). Schema: tent pole has scope field ('global' or 'thread') and optional thread_id field (set when scope='thread'). Jasper reads both global and current-thread tent poles into context. Global tent poles persist across all conversations. Per-thread tent poles only loaded for their originating thread. get_tent_poles tool accepts scope filter ('all', 'global', 'thread') and thread_id parameter.
todos.notes: Enforced hybrid scope in Pydantic and storage validators: global entries cannot carry thread IDs, thread entries require one, and all/current-thread reads combine global entries only with the selected thread. Jasper tools derive thread identity from run-scoped context rather than process globals.

todos.content: DECISION: Auto-offer at message threshold (20+ messages in conversation) + manual trigger anytime via /tentpoles command. When threshold reached, Jasper's system prompt instructs it to offer: 'I've noticed we've discussed several things — would you like me to summarize the key points?' Jasper extracts key points in response text, user reviews/approves, Jasper calls set_tent_pole for approved items. Manual trigger: user types /tentpoles, Jasper immediately proposes. Collaborative, not silent — user always in the loop.
todos.notes: Implemented deterministic /tentpoles proposal prompting and a persisted one-time offer at 20 human/assistant messages; tool messages do not inflate the threshold. Jasper is explicitly forbidden to persist silently and may call set_tent_pole only after approval. Unit tests cover manual, threshold, one-time, and tool-message behavior.

sections.title: UI Performance — Slow/Freeze Diagnosis and Fix Plan

todos.content: Diagnose and document root causes of UI slowness and freezing during agent responses. Three root causes identified: (1) No throttle on stream state updates — every LLM token triggers immediate React re-render. (2) MarkdownText re-parses entire accumulated content on every render — ReactMarkdown with remarkGfm + remarkMath + rehypeKatex is expensive per render. (3) onCustomEvent handler adds 'custom' to streamMode for ALL requests including Jasper — server sends custom events even when no agent emits them, adding SSE overhead.
todos.notes: Root causes found via LangGraph SDK source code analysis. StreamManager (manager.js) processes every token: messages.slice() copies full array, creates new state object, calls notifyListeners. With throttle:50 added, renders batched but state mutations still run per-token. callbackStreamMode (stream.lgp.js:146) auto-adds 'custom' mode when onCustomEvent is set — overhead on every request.

todos.content: Add throttle:50 to useTypedStream options in Stream.tsx. Batches React re-renders to max once per 50ms instead of every token. Applied — verify it helps with fast cloud models.
todos.notes: Added to Stream.tsx:112. Throttle batches renders but not state mutations. SDK source: StreamManager.subscribe (manager.js:287) uses setTimeout to defer listener calls. Helps but does not solve the core issue of per-token object creation.

todos.content: Consider increasing throttle from 50ms to 100-200ms. Reduces render frequency from 20fps to 5-10fps. Still smooth for reading streaming text but halves markdown re-parse cost. Simple one-line change in Stream.tsx.
todos.notes: Throttle increased from 50ms to 150ms in Stream.tsx:112. Verified in code during Phase 2 audit — value is already 150. Reconciled from pending to completed.

todos.content: Remove the onCustomEvent 'text' handler in Stream.tsx:128-129. Currently calls options.mutate() for every OpenCode text chunk, setting opencode_status='streaming' hundreds of times per second. The 'text' events are already streamed via messages stream mode. Only keep handlers for 'status', 'complete', 'error' events.
todos.notes: The 'text' branch is already removed from onCustomEvent in Stream.tsx. Handler now only covers 'complete' and 'error' events. Verified during Phase 2 audit. Reconciled from pending to completed.

todos.content: Instrument the LangGraph stream path and fix event-mode selection. todos.notes: Replaced the former unbounded status path with the versioned Deep Agents coding contract. Native stream events are translated once; canonical final messages remain separate. Text batches at 512 characters and 16 KiB, backend events cap at 128, browser retention caps at 32, duplicate sequences are ignored, and custom mutations apply only to validated coding_event version 1 envelopes. The maximum-contract browser profile completes in 447 ms with a 54 ms maximum long task. Standard LangGraph HITL interrupts remain on the resumable message stream.

todos.content: Prevent historical message rows and unrelated controls from rerendering on every stream-state update. Split stream state into narrow subscriptions or pass stable derived data into memoized components; verify with profiler render counts rather than relying on React.memo alone.

todos.content: Profile Markdown, syntax highlighting, math, and tool-call rendering separately. Cache finalized message output, keep streaming rendering lightweight, dynamically load math/highlighting code when truly needed, and avoid reparsing unchanged historical messages.
todos.notes: Streaming text uses a lightweight whitespace-preserving element. Final Markdown remains memoized. The default is the tool-capable local ollama/qwen3.5:27b model with bounded context/output settings; a production-subgraph smoke test completed with read_file and tool-result events. Cloud auth uses OLLAMA_API_KEY with the existing LLM_API_KEY as a compatibility fallback, and Hugging Face uses the library-standard HUGGINGFACEHUB_API_TOKEN. Added only variable names to .env.example, installed and locked deepagents 0.7.0b2 and langchain-huggingface 1.2.2, and added deterministic provider-selection tests. No credential values were read or displayed. Credential-dependent cloud/HF live-model validation remains part of deep-agents-parity-verification.

todos.content: Implement a Deep Agents coding subgraph behind a provider-neutral coding-agent interface. Accept messages, absolute workspace, selected model, execution mode, and thread identity; return standard LangGraph messages and structured coding events. Keep the current OpenCode subgraph available only behind a temporary rollback flag until parity is proven.
todos.notes: Implemented backend/src/coding_agent.py and routed the supervisor through a provider-neutral coding node with coding_session_id, coding_status, coding_events, execution_mode, and thread_identity. Deep Agents is the default; CODING_AGENT_BACKEND=opencode is the temporary rollback switch and maps legacy sessions at the adapter boundary. The Deep Agents backend requires an existing absolute directory, confines FilesystemBackend to that root in virtual mode, allows reads, denies writes, exposes no shell tool, emits bounded status/tool summaries, and sanitizes invalid-workspace, dependency, timeout, and provider failures. The production subgraph completed a read-only local Ollama smoke test with a tool call/result and preserved thread identity. Backend lint passed and the full suite passed 68/68.

todos.content: Configure workspace confinement, filesystem permissions, shell policy, and human-in-the-loop approval before enabling writes or command execution. Resolve and validate the absolute workspace root, deny traversal and sensitive paths, use explicit command policies, redact subprocess/tool errors, and test approve, edit, reject, cancel, and timeout flows.
todos.notes: Implemented the security boundary in backend/src/coding_agent.py and backend/src/secure_coding_tools.py and documented it in backend/SECURITY.md. read_only remains the default and legacy live/async values cannot enable mutations. Exact approval mode exposes only workspace-confined write/edit tools and an argv-only command tool, each behind standard Deep Agents/LangGraph approve-edit-reject interrupts with a 900-second expiry. Built-in writes remain denied; reads block .env, .git, and private-key formats; mutations additionally block AGENTS.md and SSH/AWS/GPG paths, traversal, sensitive files, symlink escapes, missing parents, and content over 1 MB. Writes are atomic. Commands reject shell syntax, destructive Git actions, absolute/parent/symlink escapes, risky Git/rg options, and unlisted executables; they run with no inherited credentials, bounded time/output, and credential redaction. LocalShellBackend is not used. Cancellation propagates, runtime/command/approval timeouts are bounded, edited actions are revalidated, and the OpenCode rollback adapter can no longer auto-approve. Full backend lint passed and tests passed 91/91, covering approve, edit, reject, cancellation, runtime timeout, approval expiry, command timeout, redaction, and path policies. Limitation: approved tests/package scripts execute repository code locally and are not OS-isolated; unattended or untrusted execution remains prohibited until a real sandbox is added. Durable approval/checkpoint storage remains tracked by deep-agents-persistence-memory.

todos.content: Map Deep Agents thread persistence, conversation compaction, agent memory, skills, and subagent state onto the existing LangGraph/Postgres lifecycle. Ensure one UI thread resumes the correct coding session, prevent memory leakage across repositories or users, and define reset/export behavior.
todos.notes: Implemented backend/src/coding_persistence.py and documented the lifecycle in backend/PERSISTENCE.md. The outer LangGraph server remains canonical UI conversation memory; nested Deep Agents tool, summary, subagent, and pending-HITL state uses an async durable checkpointer. Default storage is backend/data/deep_agents_checkpoints.sqlite3 so restart durability does not depend on Docker; CODING_CHECKPOINT_DB_URI selects the installed async Postgres saver when a deployment provides a dedicated URI. Session IDs are opaque SHA-256 scopes over user identity, UI thread, and resolved repository, preventing cross-user/repository reuse without embedding raw identities or paths. Deep Agents receives full outer history on the first coding turn and only the latest user turn after nested history exists. Repository AGENTS.md loads as read-only memory and workspace-local .agents/skills loads when present. Added scoped sidecar reset/export endpoints. Tests close and reopen the checkpointer to prove pending approval and multi-turn history recovery, verify user/repository isolation, and verify reset/export do not affect sibling sessions. Full backend lint passed and tests passed 96/96.

todos.content: Define and implement a bounded frontend event contract for coding status, text, tool calls, subagents, plans, file changes, approvals, completion, and errors. Use native LangGraph/Deep Agents streaming where possible, avoid duplicate message and custom-event text streams, and batch high-frequency updates to protect UI responsiveness.
todos.notes: Added backend/src/coding_events.py and integrated native Deep Agents astream messages/updates into a versioned coding_event envelope. Events include opaque session, monotonic per-run sequence, kind, status, and sanitized data. Transient text is batched at 512 characters, capped at 16 KiB, and never replaces or duplicates the canonical final LangGraph message transcript. Runs retain at most 128 events; frontend state retains only 32. Tool/subagent/plan/file events contain names and opaque call IDs but never arguments, outputs, prompts, file contents, or exception details. Approval events expose only counts, expiry, and decision types. Tests cover batching, caps, categorization, versioning, and secret-payload exclusion; the backend suite passes 99/99.

todos.content: Replace the OpenCode selector, OC status badge, opencode_status state, and OpenCode-specific labels with a Deep Agent coding option and provider-neutral coding status UI. Add subagent/tool progress only after the event contract is stable, and preserve approval and artifact behavior.
todos.notes: Replaced the OpenCode selector and OC badge with Deep Agent and provider-neutral Coding status. Removed opencode_status from Stream state and added typed coding events with sequence deduplication, 32-event retention, and a bounded transient preview. Added an explicit Read only / Ask to edit control that submits execution_mode. Added a synthetic 10-second browser regression proving the audio queue stays bounded. TypeScript, the optimized production build, the existing TTS play/stop test, and the new long-playback test pass.

todos.content: Record the production architecture contract, framework boundaries, security limits, accessibility requirements, provider fallback policy, and release gates for a LangChain-backed first-class visual workspace.

todos.content: Pass backend, provider-strategy, schema-drift, TypeScript, optimized build, UI, accessibility, reconnect, long-session, and performance verification before expanding to Plotly, Tree-sitter, issue-list, or architecture renderers.

Post-smoke remediation passes 121 backend tests, clean production builds, and the full 16-test mocked browser suite. Layout coverage asserts 50/50 split, divider dragging, pane containment, pinned composer, three-mode focus switching, dark contrast, malformed-data safety, long-thread performance, streaming performance, and TTS. sections.title: Explainer Session Persistence — LangGraph Threads + Store

todos.content: Write Architecture Decision Record documenting the explainer session model: durable collection of LangGraph threads and immutable visual artifacts, not one oversized chat-state object. Document thread copying via Agent Server API, LangGraph Store for session catalog, PostgreSQL checkpointer for messages and execution state, object storage for large binaries, and immutable artifact versioning with narration.
todos.notes: Added the accepted backend/EXPLAINER_SESSION_ARCHITECTURE.md ADR. It defines owner-scoped session catalogs in LangGraph Store, root and copied child Agent Server threads in PostgreSQL checkpoints, immutable content-addressed artifact manifests with parent versions and narration, object storage for large bytes, separate presentation state, idempotent crash recovery, archive/export/deletion lifecycle, additive migrations, coordinated backup/restore verification, server-side authorization, and an explicit LangSmith-observability-only boundary.

todos.content: Define versioned Pydantic schemas for ExplainerSession (session ID, title, owner, root thread ID, repo identity, artifact IDs, child thread IDs, active artifact, timestamps, schema version, retention policy) and VisualArtifact v3 (artifact ID, version, renderer, payload, grounding sources, originating thread/checkpoint/message, node narration segments, parent artifact reference, content hash). Export JSON Schema and generate matching TypeScript types.
todos.notes: Implemented frozen, strict Pydantic ExplainerSession v1 and VisualArtifact v3 contracts in backend/src/explainer_models.py, including ownership, repository identity, root/child checkpoint linkage, retention, artifact versions, inline versus object storage, grounding, origin, node narration, deterministic ordering, and verified canonical content hashes. Exported stable JSON Schemas and generated separate TypeScript contracts under agent-chat-ui/src/lib/explainer. Added schema generation/check scripts, seven model tests, Ruff validation, frontend typechecking, and stale-generation checks.

todos.content: Run persistence spike against installed Agent Server: verify thread copying via copy-thread API, checkpoint branching behavior across restarts, Store writes for session catalog and artifact manifests, thread search by explainer_session_id metadata, and PostgreSQL backup/restore with migrations.
todos.notes: Added a repeatable seed/verify/cleanup probe and recorded evidence in backend/spikes/EXPLAINER_PERSISTENCE_RESULTS.md. Against self-hosted Agent Server 0.11.2, native copy-thread produced a stateful child; exact root checkpoint, copied child, owner/session metadata search, Store catalog, and artifact manifest all survived an API-container restart. A PostgreSQL custom-format dump restored into an isolated database with identical 12 public tables, 1,937 checkpoints, two Store rows, and exact spike identities; all temporary records were cleaned. The spike also found and documented the installed API's copy-at-current-head constraint and the required compare-before-copy conflict guard.

todos.content: Add contract tests for idempotent artifact writes, crash recovery mid-exploration, server-side ownership and authorization filtering, archive/export/deletion behavior, and migration of existing legacy visuals to session-linked artifacts.
todos.notes: Implemented owner-scoped ExplainerSessionRepository lifecycle behavior over LangGraph Store: idempotent immutable artifact batches, optimistic revisions, persisted branch intents and restart recovery, active/archived catalogs, export, two-phase deletion plans, and validated legacy ConceptMapArtifact migration. Added contract coverage for hash conflicts, retry safety, crash recovery, nondisclosing cross-owner access, stale revisions, archive/export/delete, grounding and narration preservation, and storage-boundary imports. The combined explainer/visual suite passes 25 tests.

todos.content: Document and enforce separation: LangSmith tracing remains observability only, not the session database. Session state lives in PostgreSQL checkpoints and Store; artifacts live in Store; large binaries live in object storage.
todos.notes: The accepted Explainer Session ADR explicitly assigns LangSmith to observability only, Agent Server PostgreSQL checkpoints to execution state, LangGraph Store to session catalogs/manifests, and object storage to large bytes. The persistence implementation depends on BaseStore and versioned domain models only; an AST-level architecture test fails if a LangSmith runtime import enters the session database module.

todos.content: Run a read-only Tach spike against representative Python repositories and this backend. Evaluate module-boundary discovery, internal and external dependencies, public interfaces, cycles, layered architecture, monorepo/source-root behavior, output stability, performance, and failure modes. Capture local `tach map` JSON and `tach report --raw` evidence without changing analyzed repositories.
todos.notes: Installed and locked Tach 0.35.0, Grimp 3.15, Tree-sitter 0.26.0 with Python grammar 0.25.0, and Jedi 0.20.0. Ran local-only Tach against this backend and a committed representative fixture covering source roots, layers, interfaces, TYPE_CHECKING, cycles, and dynamic imports; tach show --web was never invoked. Recorded reproducible evidence and a hybrid architecture decision in backend/spikes/TACH_ARCHITECTURE_RESULTS.md. Tach map is fast and useful for static file dependencies, while configured policy is authoritative only when tach.toml exists; Grimp supplies queryable modules, cycles, externals, and line evidence.

todos.content: Implement a deterministic adapter from Tach's local dependency output into the renderer-neutral grounded graph schema. Represent packages, modules, architectural boundaries, internal/external dependencies, interfaces, cycles, source paths, and line-level evidence where available. Preserve claim provenance and do not allow the model, ELK, or React Flow to invent relationships.
todos.notes: Implemented strict content-addressed canonical architecture contracts and a local TachArchitectureAdapter. It enumerates confined Python source files, validates every Tach path against the repository root, records file hashes and config provenance, separates observed Tach-map imports from declared tach.toml modules/dependencies/layers/interfaces, detects and marks cycles, emits explicit unconfigured diagnostics, sanitizes CLI failures, and produces deterministic immutable graphs. DerivedLayout and PresentationState are separate hash-linked models so ELK/React Flow cannot mutate facts. Added six passing trust-boundary/determinism tests. External packages and import-line enrichment remain assigned to the Grimp validation task because Tach does not output them.

todos.content: Add progressive Python symbol drill-down below the Tach module view using Tree-sitter for syntax-grounded symbols and source ranges plus Jedi for static inference and reference resolution. Map results into a versioned Python visualization profile with stable architectural kinds and modifiers instead of exposing a raw syntax tree.
todos.notes: Implemented on-demand PythonSymbolAdapter drill-down. Tree-sitter supplies observed class/function/method source ranges and stable qualified identities; it classifies dataclasses, protocols, enums, exceptions, visibility, async/generator/decorator/property/static/class/abstract/test modifiers without exposing a raw syntax tree. Jedi supplies bounded same-file reference edges and inferred identity metadata explicitly labeled as inferred, with failures degrading safely and parser cache confined to OS temporary storage. Added versioned frozen Python visualization styles/icon roles and four tests for classification, references, source provenance, syntax-error recovery, determinism, and profile immutability. The full Python pipeline suite passes 14 tests.

todos.content: Compare Tach dependency results with Grimp's queryable ImportGraph on the same fixtures. Document disagreements, dynamic-import limitations, namespace-package behavior, TYPE_CHECKING imports, unresolved dependencies, and the conditions under which Grimp should be used as an embedded fallback or validation oracle.
todos.notes: Implemented GrimpArchitectureValidator as a queryable validation and enrichment layer over the immutable Tach graph. It restores sys.path after confined analysis, respects tach.toml source roots and TYPE_CHECKING policy, supports namespace packages, adds observed package/module/external nodes, records exact import-line evidence, compares internal Tach/Grimp edges, emits explicit disagreements, captures cycle breakers, and diagnoses runtime-computed imports without inventing their targets. Four tests cover matching graphs, forced disagreement, namespace packages, unavailable externals, TYPE_CHECKING exclusion, dynamic imports, path restoration, and deterministic output. The spike report documents when Grimp is the validation oracle versus Tach's declared-policy authority.

todos.content: Feed only validated canonical Python architecture graphs into ELK for layered positioning and edge routing, then render them through React Flow with deterministic Python styles, accessible labels, node selection, narration highlighting, drill-down, and conversation branching. Verify that re-layout and presentation changes cannot mutate factual graph content.
todos.notes: Implemented immutable ArchitectureGraph v1 validation and browser hash verification, ELK layered/orthogonal derived layout, deterministic accessible React Flow Python nodes and evidence-aware edges, narration highlight/replay, grounded drill-down, and actual LangGraph thread-copy branching with session/artifact/node/checkpoint provenance metadata. Layout failure falls back to a factual outline without mutating graph content. Backend contract tests (22 passed), production Next build, typecheck/lint, and nine Playwright visual-workspace tests passed, including tamper rejection and branch creation.

sections.title: Jasper Supervisor — Shared Deep Agents Runtime

todos.content: Write an Architecture Decision Record for a single LangChain Deep Agents runtime with Jasper as the primary human-facing supervisor and Jasper, Research, Coding, and Explainer as strongly configured profiles. Preserve the existing outer LangGraph thread, checkpoint, routing, and interrupt lifecycle; define when a profile is directly selected versus delegated as a subagent; and explicitly reject separate duplicated agent runtimes.
todos.notes: Added backend/JASPER_SUPERVISOR_ARCHITECTURE.md. The accepted ADR defines one shared Deep Agents implementation foundation with independently compiled capability-scoped profiles; preserves the outer LangGraph lifecycle; routes unselected requests deterministically to Jasper; keeps explicit profile selection authoritative; uses native structured delegation; retains Coding as a separately sandboxed compiled subagent; defines permission, approval, persistence, voice, citation, migration, rollback, and release-gate boundaries; preserves Magic Coder until a separate migration; and defers Tent Poles implementation without discarding its collaborative-memory requirements.

todos.content: Define versioned Pydantic configuration contracts and a shared agent factory for Jasper, Research, Coding, and Explainer profiles. Each profile must declare identity and communication style, allowed tools, skills, memory scope, backend, filesystem and network permissions, structured response format, approval policy, delegation policy, voice-delivery metadata, and provider/model capability requirements.
todos.notes: Implemented backend/src/agent_profiles.py with strict versioned Pydantic contracts for Jasper, Research, Coding, Explainer, and the independent Fact-Checker plus a shared DeepAgentProfileFactory. Contracts declare tools, capabilities, backend, filesystem/network/memory policy, HITL approvals, delegation, voice delivery, resource limits, model requirements, and structured response names. Factory construction fails closed on undeclared tools, host expansion, backend mismatch, unauthorized delegation, or missing high-risk interrupts; Coding remains an independently compiled sandbox profile. Added 13 focused tests in backend/tests/test_agent_profiles.py; Ruff and all focused tests pass.

todos.content: Implement Jasper's deterministic handle-or-delegate policy using Deep Agents subagent support while keeping explicit human profile selection authoritative. Add typed delegation envelopes, bounded context handoff, cancellation, timeout and retry behavior, subagent result provenance, conflict detection, approval interrupts, and one coherent Jasper-authored final response synthesized from specialist results.
todos.notes: Implemented deterministic explicit-profile routing and native Deep Agents delegation. Added bounded typed delegation/result/provenance/conflict contracts, retry/timeout/cancellation behavior, Jasper synthesis ownership, specialist call limits, and direct routing without obsolete generic handoff approvals. High-risk Coding mutations remain interrupted at the actual tool boundary.

todos.content: Enforce profile security through tool withholding, Deep Agents backend permissions, sandboxing, network isolation, secret exclusion, and human-in-the-loop middleware. Give Research network tools without repository writes; give Explainer read-only grounded architecture tools; give Coding a sandboxed selected workspace with approval-gated write, execute, git, and external network operations; and prevent Jasper from silently expanding a delegated profile's authority.
todos.notes: Enforced profile authority in DeepAgentProfileFactory and compiled boundaries: undeclared tools and hosts fail closed; Research and Fact-Checker have fixed-host read-only network tools and no repository access; Explainer is filesystem-denied with grounded read tools; Coding retains selected-workspace sandboxing and HITL mutation tools; Jasper has no direct network tools. Existing traversal, symlink, secret, approval-bypass, and workspace-isolation tests remain green.

todos.content: Implement user-scoped persistent Deep Agents memory for communication, learning, voice, and workflow preferences using LangGraph Store-backed namespaces. Keep organization and security policy memory read-only, separate learned preferences from authoritative policy, audit memory writes, and link Jasper, specialist child threads, immutable visual artifacts, bookmarks, and narration through the durable ExplainerSession model.
todos.notes: Implemented owner-scoped LangGraph Store preference namespaces, audited atomic writes, read-only organization policy, and explicit links to thread, ExplainerSession, artifact, source message, narration, and bookmark identities. Jasper receives the authenticated runtime Store; cross-user isolation and session linkage are contract-tested. LangSmith remains observability only.

todos.content: Define a renderer-neutral narration contract that separates voice-friendly text from visual artifacts and stores speaker profile, narration segments, node associations, pace, pause, emphasis, bookmark, replay, and user-preference metadata. Map this contract at playback time to capabilities supported by Pocket TTS or future engines instead of storing SSML as canonical session content.
todos.notes: Added renderer-neutral NarrationTrack/NarrationCue contracts with speaker profile, ordered segments, node links, pace, pauses, emphasis, bookmarks, replay, and user preference metadata. Playback capability adaptation maps canonical cues to Pocket TTS or future engines without persisting SSML. Browser tests cover node highlighting, replay, and grounded branch follow-up.

todos.content: Migrate Jasper, Research, Coding, and Explainer incrementally behind the shared Deep Agents factory without a broad rewrite. Preserve stable UI agent IDs and existing thread compatibility, remove superseded duplicate agent loops only after profile parity is proven, and provide migrations for existing threads, profile metadata, approvals, artifacts, and saved user preferences.
todos.notes: Migrated Jasper, Research, Coding, Explainer, and Fact-Checker behind the shared factory/compiled-subagent boundary while preserving outer LangGraph lifecycle and stable UI IDs. Added an additive idempotent legacy-thread migration for Deep Agent/OpenCode identifiers that preserves messages, approvals, artifacts, sessions, and preference links and documents field-level rollback. Research now uses the same compiled verified pipeline for direct and Jasper-delegated work.

todos.content: Add unit, contract, integration, browser, security, persistence, restart-recovery, cancellation, provider-capability, latency, memory-pressure, and end-to-end tests for the shared runtime and all profiles. Verify explicit profile selection, Jasper delegation and synthesis, HITL resume, cross-thread memory isolation, explainer-session recovery, voice metadata fallback, Ollama local and cloud plus Hugging Face routing, and that cloud-profile use never loads a local Ollama model unexpectedly.
todos.notes: Passed the production gate across backend unit/contract/integration/security/persistence/restart/cancellation/provider tests, frontend type checking/lint/build/schema checks, and the full Playwright suite. Coverage includes explicit selection, delegation, HITL resume, memory isolation, ExplainerSession recovery, voice fallback, Ollama local/cloud and Hugging Face routing, cloud endpoint isolation, bounded streaming, UI latency, long-playback memory pressure, and operational migration rollback.

todos.content: Implement a dual-channel citation contract for Jasper and Research output. Voice-friendly narration must refer naturally to stable numbered references, such as 'according to reference one,' without reading URLs, citation JSON, or structured metadata aloud. Simultaneously render a numbered, accessible, clickable reference panel containing the full canonical URL, title, publisher or author, publication date when known, relevant excerpt, retrieval timestamp, claim associations, and one-action navigation to the source.
todos.notes: Implemented strict dual-channel Pydantic and TypeScript contracts: URL-free voice narration, stable contiguous reference numbers, claim/reference integrity, canonical HTTPS links, title/author/date/excerpt/retrieval metadata, and accessible one-action reference navigation. The UI renders citations and independent verification separately from speech; replay numbering and malformed-response rejection are tested.

todos.content: Add a permission-limited Fact-Checker Deep Agents subagent that independently decomposes research output into checkable claims, retrieves corroborating and contradictory evidence without relying only on the Research agent's selected sources, evaluates source provenance using documented lateral-reading criteria informed by SIFT and the P.R.O.V.E.N. source-evaluation process, and returns structured per-claim verification results to Jasper before final synthesis.
todos.notes: Implemented a filesystem-denied Fact-Checker Deep Agent with structured SIFT+PROVEN per-claim verdicts, calibrated coverage confidence, evidence for/against, independence flag, and methodology notes. The compiled Research pipeline invokes it deterministically before returning to Jasper. Research-selected evidence IDs are excluded through a ContextVar-enforced tool boundary, not prompt compliance, and visual confidence output is tested.

todos.content: Implement typed, read-only Research tools for authoritative scholarly discovery and metadata retrieval through Semantic Scholar, arXiv, PubMed via NCBI E-utilities, and IEEE Xplore. Normalize results into one evidence schema containing stable identifiers, canonical links, bibliographic metadata, abstract or permitted excerpt, source provider, query provenance, access status, and licensing constraints; rank by relevance and evidence quality rather than treating provider inclusion as proof of a claim.
todos.notes: Implemented fixed-host read-only Semantic Scholar, arXiv, PubMed/NCBI, IEEE Xplore, and clearly labeled lower-authority Tavily fallback connectors. All normalize stable IDs, canonical links, bibliographic metadata, permitted excerpts, access/license/provenance, publication status, transparent evidence-quality factors, and untrusted-text marking. Added bounded TTL caching, connection retries, rate-limit/outage statuses, redirect refusal, cross-provider deduplication, retraction/correction penalties, paywall handling, and secret-exclusion tests.

todos.content: Add contract and end-to-end tests for Deep Agents Research and Fact-Checker orchestration, structured confidence output, source independence, claim-to-reference linkage, citation-number stability, spoken-versus-visual separation, dead or redirected URLs, duplicate records across providers, retractions and corrections, contradictory evidence, paywalls, empty results, rate limits, provider failure, prompt injection in retrieved text, and session replay with bookmarks.
todos.notes: Added contract, integration, and browser coverage for native compiled Research/Fact-Checker orchestration, confidence calibration, enforced source independence, claim links, replay-stable numbering, voice/visual separation, redirects, duplicates, retractions/corrections, contradictory evidence schema, paywalls, empty/rate-limited/provider-failure states, untrusted prompt-injection text, bookmarks, and restored-session rendering. Final full backend and Playwright gates pass.

todos.content: Allow the human to attach an explicitly selected EPUB without granting Jasper filesystem or directory access, validate the publication container, and provide bounded extracted publication content with source structure.
todos.notes: Implemented the operating-system file picker as the authorization boundary for EPUB. Extension-aware detection accepts legitimate .epub files even when the browser reports an empty or generic MIME type. A bounded read-only sidecar adapter validates the EPUB container, rejects encryption, unsafe paths, malformed metadata, oversized entries, excessive expansion, and excess entry counts, removes script/style content, and returns publication metadata, chapter source labels, content-profile information, and capped extracted text. Agent Chat UI converts that result into LangChain's documented PlainText content block; Jasper receives no absolute path or directory authority. Validation passed: 136 backend tests, TypeScript, production build, and 10 UI-control browser tests. Governance reference: GOVERNANCE_FRAMEWORK.md.
